co_floyd_hill_saddleback_mt.blurb: A scattering of boulders on the slopes of Saddleback Mountain above Floyd Hill, on the upper edge of the Clear Creek Canyon bouldering zone at roughly 8,400 feet. Problems run from V1 up to V10, with the heart of the grades in V4 through V6, and a couple of tall, hard lines such as Exodus and Exodus Low draw the strong climbers. Access is by a narrow dirt road that climbs through a residential neighborhood, so this is a quiet, low-profile spot: drive slowly, keep noise and dogs at home, and be considerate of the people who live along the road. Much of the hillside above is private land that is not well marked, so confirm boundaries before wandering.

co_b_cactus_cliff_left_muscle_beach_righ.blurb: The left side of Cactus Cliff, a tall, sunny limestone wall at Shelf Road near Canon City. Nearly all of the climbing here is bolted sport on steep, sharp, pocketed rock, with grades from the 5.8s up through the 5.12s and the largest cluster in the low-to-mid 5.12 range, so it suits strong 5.11 and 5.12 climbers best. Muscle Beach is the signature line, with Hot Beach, Tits Up and The French Are Here close by. The wall soaks up sun, which makes it a favorite on cold days and a hot one in summer. Expect company on good weekends.
co_b_cactus_cliff_left_muscle_beach_righ.parking_note: Leave the car in the large lot at The Bank and walk from there; the cliff sits just around the corner from the campground.
co_b_cactus_cliff_left_muscle_beach_righ.approach: From the Bank lot, take the path on the right side of the road heading northwest, drop into the drainage and cross its bottom, then turn uphill on the road and pick up the trail that runs along the base of the cliff.

co_dungeon_the_2.blurb: A steep, shaded wall on the west side of Staunton Rocks in Staunton State Park, southwest of Denver. It holds a handful of long, overhanging lines of both sport and trad, mostly in the 5.12 and 5.13 range with a few 5.10s to warm up on, and the rock is a notch below the neighboring Tan Corridor though the movement is fun. The face stays in shade until mid-afternoon and some lines are shaded all day, so it works well when other cliffs are baking. Bring a light rack and a knee pad or two for the steeper routes.
co_dungeon_the_2.parking_note: Most climbers start at the Lazy V lot inside Staunton State Park; if it is full, use the Meadow lot nearer the entrance and accept a longer hike in.
co_dungeon_the_2.approach: About two miles on a good trail with little elevation gain. From the Lazy V lot, join the Staunton Ranch trail, turn left to the signed climber access trail, then follow cairns to the base of the wall.

co_redgarden_roof_routes.blurb: A band of steep climbs at the base of Redgarden Wall in Eldorado Canyon, all starting beneath a long south-facing roof. Each route follows the same pattern: delicate, solid face climbing for the first 40 to 60 feet, a roof of about ten feet, then exposed face above with thin protection. Grades sit almost entirely between 5.11 and 5.12, so this is not a place for climbers below that level. Mixed trad, sport and aid lines share the wall, with The Wisdom, Guenese and Evangeline among the most appealing. The lower section can stay climbable in light weather.
co_redgarden_roof_routes.approach: Cross the footbridge, walk west along the base of the Whale's Tail, and head right at the fork onto the switchbacks. Climb until you are near the start of Tower Two, then angle up and left to the base of the roof.

_expect.name: West Ridge - part B - Long John to Verschneidung

co_west_ridge_part_b_long_john_to_versch.blurb: A stretch of the West Ridge in Eldorado Canyon State Park, across the creek from the main road. The West Ridge is known for short, aesthetic crack and corner climbs, and this section is nearly all traditional, with grades spread from the easy 5th class through the 5.11s and the biggest group around 5.9 and 5.10. Long John Wall, Chianti, Break on Through and The Unsaid are the lines to look for. Sandstone here rewards careful gear placement, and old fixed protection should be backed up. A bridge keeps the walk-in short, which makes it a good place for several quick pitches in a day.

co_wendell_spire.blurb: A sunny, protected wall in Castlewood Canyon State Park on the plains southeast of Denver, often described as the warmest crag in Colorado. The rock is the conglomerate typical of the canyon, and the climbing is almost all bolted sport with a single trad line. A few easy routes exist, but most of the grades fall between 5.11 and 5.12, with some 5.13 and 5.14 projects that give it a reputation among strong climbers. The Black Streak and Kronos are the hard testpieces, while Cobble Wobble and Nob Job are friendlier. Cobbles can pull out, so test holds, and expect rattlesnakes in warm months.

co_risk_area_the.blurb: A section of the Golden Cliffs on North Table Mountain, just outside Golden. The cliff band is volcanic lava rock, and the climbing here is a mix of trad lines, bolted sport routes and top-rope laps, mostly short and single pitch. Grades start in the 5.5 range and reach 5.12, with the bulk of routes between 5.7 and 5.11. The cliffs catch plenty of sun, which makes them a comfortable choice on cold days, but rattlesnakes are a concern in summer and fall, and the rock can feel polished or greasy when warm. Two trails climb from the parking lots to the cliffs.
co_risk_area_the.parking_note: Use the lower Peery Parkway lot first, or the North Table Mountain Park lot off CO 93; each has a trail up the hill to the cliffs.

co_wind_tower_sw_face.blurb: The southwest face of the Wind Tower in Eldorado Canyon State Park, one of the best places in the canyon for lower-grade traditional climbing. Every route is trad, and most grades fall between 5.7 and 5.9, with a few easier and a few harder lines up to the 5.10s and 5.12. Reggae and Tagger are standouts here. The first couple of pitches have excellent rock, but higher up it sees less traffic and can be loose. The most popular routes often have a line of parties waiting, so start early or pick a less obvious line.

co_monument_canyon.blurb: The canyon below Independence Monument in Colorado National Monument near Grand Junction, a landscape of red sandstone towers and walls. Climbing is mostly traditional and multipitch, with a smaller share of aid lines, a few sport routes and some boulder problems. Grades center on 5.9 through 5.11 and reach 5.12, with Wizard I, Desert Solitaire and Get A Life among the notable lines. The sandstone is soft and fragile, so it should be dry before anyone climbs, and gear is less reliable when it is wet. Summers are hot; the comfortable months run from fall through spring.

co_12_beijing_aka_beyond_the_2150_wall.blurb: A wall at The Bank, one of the busiest sectors of Shelf Road near Canon City. The rock is the sharp, pocketed limestone that Shelf is known for, and the routes are almost all bolted sport, with grades from the 5.6s to the low 5.12s and most of them in the 5.10 to 5.11 range. Beijing, Crazy as Me, Restless and The Lucky One are the lines to start with. The Bank gets warm sun and works well in winter, though it can feel hot in summer. Bring hand salve for the sharp rock.
co_12_beijing_aka_beyond_the_2150_wall.parking_note: Park in the big lot at The Bank, beside the campground, rather than along the road.
